content: The metabolism of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is significantly influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The following are detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration with other drugs: 1. Rifapentine: This drug decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 2. Rilpivirine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals, including rilpivirine. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of toxicity. 4. Sildenafil: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Chronic administration of sildenafil for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is contraindicated. For erectile dysfunction (ED), the dose should not exceed 25 mg within 48 hours. 5. Simvastatin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events. 6. St. John’s Wort: This herbal supplement decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 7. Tenofovir DF: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals, including tenofovir DF. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Tipranavir: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals, including tipranavir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Voclosporin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases voclosporin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Zidovudine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals, including zidovudine. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Acalabrutinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 12. Adagrasib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases adagrasib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, co-administration may increase adagrasib toxicity. 13. Ado-trastuzumab emtansine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases DM1 (the cytotoxic component of ado-trastuzumab emtansine) levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to increased risk of toxicity. 14. Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 15. Bedaquiline: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 16. Betibeglogene autotemcel: Antiretroviral medications, including elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, should not be taken for at least one month before mobilization or during the expected duration of elimination of the medications. ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 17. Brigatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases brigatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 18. Cabozantinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases cabozantinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor is required, decrease the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 19. Capivasertib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases capivasertib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Ceritinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 21. Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 22. Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Copanlisib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 24. Dabrafenib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 25. Daridorexant: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 26. Edoxaban: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases edoxaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustment may be required. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 27. Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 28. Elacestrant: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 29. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with certain strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Elivaldogene autotemcel: Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of elivaldogene autotemcel. 31. Enasidenib: Avoid co-administration of enasidenib with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, decrease the substrate dosage per prescribing information. 32. Encorafenib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 33. Etravirine: Etravirine decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 34. Fexinidazole: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF decreases fexinidazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 35. Futibatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases futibatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 36. Glasdegib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases glasdegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider alternative therapies or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 37. Ibrutinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 38. Idelalisib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases idelalisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust dosage as needed. 39. Indinavir: Indinavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 41. Ketamine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ketamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 42. Lefamulin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lefamulin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 43. Lemborexant: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 44. Leniolisib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases leniolisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 45. Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 46. Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. 47. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel: Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. 48. Lurbinectedin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration.
